verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between Ergosta-4,24(28)-dien-3-one and Ataxin-2, mediated through the Dehydrogenase/reductase SDR family member 9. This compound is identified as a target of two different molecules: one is (1R,2S,6R,7R,10S,11R,12R,14S)-10,11-dihydroxy-2,6-dimethyl-12-propan-2-yl-13-oxatetracyclo[8.5.0.02,7.012,14]pentadecane-6-carboxylic acid, which in turn targets Ataxin-2. The second molecule, Ajugaciliatin E, also targets Ataxin-2 through the same intermediate. The scores for both pathways are consistent, indicating a plausible biological link between Ergosta-4,24(28)-dien-3-one and Ataxin-2. The mechanism appears to involve the SDR family member 9 as a central mediator, suggesting that Ergosta-4,24(28)-dien-3-one may act as a modulator or activator of this pathway. The evidence supports a potential functional relationship, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and the role of Ergosta-4,24(28)-dien-3-one in the regulation of Ataxin-2.
